### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/service-automation`, touching **8** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/kernel/cluster.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via AutomationEngine (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **11** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d2bc1ffdc36412da08a7ff40350302b991aeef6f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `5c45e0c37239dd9c16c4605dcefcd8c86f60f081` — the merge of head `18e9316c4d30cf56c9302b7f87d67ad71d9bdc08` into base `d2bc1ffdc36412da08a7ff40350302b991aeef6f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 5c45e0c37239dd9c16c4605dcefcd8c86f60f081 && git checkout 5c45e0c37239dd9c16c4605dcefcd8c86f60f081
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin d2bc1ffdc36412da08a7ff40350302b991aeef6f 18e9316c4d30cf56c9302b7f87d67ad71d9bdc08 && git checkout -B drift-repro d2bc1ffdc36412da08a7ff40350302b991aeef6f && git merge --no-ff 18e9316c4d30cf56c9302b7f87d67ad71d9bdc08

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d2bc1ffdc36412da08a7ff40350302b991aeef6f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs d2bc1ffdc36412da08a7ff40350302b991aeef6f` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT (L1-a) · repo:objectstack#1 · head `18e9316c4d30cf56c9302b7f87d67ad71d9bdc08` · 2026-11-19T18:58Z

- **形态**
  - Draft, base `main`, 4 commits, 5 files, +214/−20. Merge-base `e35cf035`, no main merge.
  - `check-governed-merges.mjs --pr 35627`: NOT governed.
  - The body carries `Fixes #35369`, `Clause-②: no` and `Metadata-protocol: none`. The changeset is a `@objectstack/service-automation` patch.
  - The file surface matches claim 7016179676 plus amendment 7018333993. That amendment covers `dag-traversal.ts` passing the judge's `code` through, and `engine.ts` (the private return type only).
- **The card's Expected is met.** `validateFlowExpressions` decides "is this a braces-rule refusal" at every `refuse()` call site. The new fifth parameter is required, so the compiler leaves no site undecided. The old header is emitted byte-for-byte only when one such refusal is listed; otherwise the neutral count header is used. Every listed line is unchanged.
- **The per-site classification, read on this head**
  - **Expression-judge errors** (predicate, flow text slot, node text slot): `isBraceRuleCode(e.code)` over `cel-template-brace`, `template-single-brace`, `cel-dialect-mismatch` and `template-dialect-mismatch`.
    - I read the whole `ExprValidationCode` table in `expression-refusal.ts`. No other code speaks to braces or a dialect.
    - The date-text, type-mismatch, unknown-function and parse codes correctly fall outside.
  - **Retired `{…}` value-slot tokens** (`flowNodeValueTemplateRefusals`): always `true`. All of them are brace tokens.
  - **Text-slot token refusals**: `textSlotRefusalIsSingleBrace` tests whether the refusal starts with `TEXT_SLOT_TEMPLATE_REFUSAL`.
    - `textSlotTemplateRefusal` joins the single-brace refusal first and the unbound-`$` hole refusal second (`flow-text-slot-template.ts`, and its docblock says so).
    - The hole sentence does not begin with that constant. So a text with both kinds is `true`, and a hole-only text is `false`.
  - **Value envelopes**: a judge error goes by its code. A shape refusal (which has no code) is `true` only when the envelope names a dialect other than `cel`. A missing or blank `source` is `false`. A shape failure with several issues flags every issue, but the header decision is per list, so the outcome is the same.
  - **Structural, blank-source and predicate-shape refusals**: `false`.
- **Pins and ablations**
  - The new describe has 9 cases: date-text alone, unknown function alone and an unbound `$` hole alone each get the neutral header; a braced predicate alone gets the braces header; and a mix is covered, with each line byte-identical to its solo listing. Further cases cover the envelope arms.
  - Three ablations went red and each restore was proven: header forced to braces (3 red), envelope kind forced non-brace (1 red), and envelope code arm forced non-brace (1 red).
  - The package suite is 4195/4195 and the typecheck passes (os-dev-report 7018287017).
  - The one prose reference outside the package, a comment in `spec/automation/flow.test.ts:1241`, quotes the braces header for a braced edge condition. That header is still emitted, so the comment stays true.
- nit (accepted): `refuse()`'s docblock says the kind is "never read back out of its sentence". The text-slot arm reads a prefix, but the prefix is the spec's published lead constant, and the order is a documented contract. That is fine.
- **Accepted deviations**
  - The neutral header carries no ADR citation. That is right, because a date-text verdict is not an ADR-0032 §1a parse error.
  - No HTTP code is asserted, because `registerFlow` throws a plain `Error`.
  - One gate family is NOT MEASURED locally (exit 3, shallow checkout), and CI runs it.
- **门禁** — on this head: 39 success, 18 skipped, 0 failure. Mergeable `clean`.
- **落地条款** — not governed and no L2 face: b1-C lands this head. A new push needs a fresh L1 only if it changes more than a main merge.
